items.excerpt: Figma's Data Science team assumed AI saves users time, but quantifying it required a new approach to research design. The post details the methodology behind measuring real time savings from Figma Make.

Screenshot prompting has a ceiling: paste a design and the model makes a plausible approximation. The author builds a deterministic Figma-to-Claude Code handoff pipeline that feeds structured design data instead of pixels.

ArtStation and Sketchfab have been sold, creating an integrated ecosystem spanning the whole creative process. Creative Bloq weighs what the merger means for digital artists' portfolios, licensing and AI exposure.

AI coding tools are excellent at answering the current request but forget everything else. The piece argues the design system — tokens, component contracts — is the persistent memory layer AI-assisted frontend teams are missing.

When building a highly interactive, tactile web experience, the architecture must serve the art direction. Alexey Kopytin explains the architectural rationale behind a digital stress-relief squeeze toy built with Lottie, DOM events and distance-based logic.

Every agent-generated frontend looks the same. The author names the 'AI Design Fingerprint' and shows how to break it by forcing intentional design decisions through structured reasoning instead of default prompting.

A design-lens reading of Star Wars' droids as a model for AI interaction: character, constraint and legibility over chat boxes. UX Collective uses the fiction to argue for how AI products should behave.

UX Collective's roundup on encoding designer judgment into machine-readable form: why chat is the wrong interface for AI, and the rise of Design.md files that give agents the taste rules a team already has.
Ninety years of loom engineering went into teaching machines to catch their own mistakes — a history lesson for designers building error-aware AI systems today.

Vercel Sandbox now runs on Vercel Managed Images — versioned, open-source base images bundling Node.js, Python and coding agents, so agent-driven prototyping environments start from a consistent baseline.
CG Channel's weekly roundup of tool updates you may have missed, including FumeFX 7.6 for 3ds Max, Character Control Rig 0.3.1 for Blender, and PFTrack 26.08.
Storm Studios breaks down the combat sequences for Daredevil: Born Again S2, covering digi-doubles, sparks and practical-to-digital blending across the Disney+ series.
Developer Drin built a fully animated alien with no mesh at all — the whole creature is raymarched in Three.js with shader math, a reminder of how much visual craft lives outside asset pipelines.
Cartesian Caramel recreates the web tornado from Spider-Man: Brand New Day entirely with Blender geometry nodes, showing a procedural route to blockbuster-scale VFX.
A developer brings Sea of Thieves-style stylized ocean rendering to Godot — 'so real you can almost feel the seasickness' — with a shader-driven water system.
A look at the work of 3D artist Giovane Henriques and how he experiments with colour as the primary driver of a render's mood rather than a post-process afterthought.
A primer on blend shapes in 3D animation: easy to set up and capable of very organic-feeling movement, they remain the backbone of facial performance in an era of AI-assisted rigging.

Leo AI lays out how to judge whether an AI tool actually captures engineering tribal knowledge — the undocumented design rules that live in senior engineers' heads — instead of just indexing CAD files.
Dell's new P4326QEB all-in-one 43-inch 4K conference monitor replaces separate cameras, speakers and displays in design-team huddle spaces.
Apple and MLB will livestream games to Vision Pro in Apple Immersive starting August 28th — the first regular live immersive-video production pipeline at this scale.
Martial arts simulator TaoLu uses body-tracked instruction and spatial coaching UI to turn a headset into a dojo — a case study in embodied VR interaction design.
Walkthrough of Meta's new Muse family — Muse Spark, Muse Image and Muse Video — and what the generative image/video models mean for creative production workflows.
A practical build-out of always-on ChatGPT automations: scheduled tasks, memory and connectors wired so the assistant keeps working on your projects between sessions.
